messages:
Priya Nair: quick pass on the rule-builder in staging — on a 13" laptop the threshold row wraps into 3 lines when you have a 95% burn-rate + 5min window + description. preview panel gets pushed down and you lose the channel ordering affordance. gif: https://.../wrap-issue.gif :grimacing:
Ben Howard: yeah that wrapping is rough. can we stack labels differently? e.g. move 'window' into a subtle pill and keep the numeric threshold as primary. reduces inline width. also the '+' add-channel button is visually heavy.
Juno Park: keyboard/aria note: the numeric stepper currently uses native number input but we don't announce the percent symbol. VoiceOver reads 'ninety five' which is ambiguous. aria-valuetext="95% burn rate" would fix it.
Eli Torres: copy nit: the small helper currently says "notify channels" which feels terse. prefer "Send to channels" or "Send notifications to" so it reads like an action. Also the preview header reads "Preview — matched channels" which is awkward. Maybe "Alert preview: matched channels".
Priya Nair: visual suggestion: introduce a two-column compact layout for the rule row: left: metric + threshold, right: window + preview/actions. On collapse, show a single-line summary chip that expands on hover.
Ben Howard: idea for channel ordering: give each channel a drag handle and expose an overflow menu for infrequent ones. show a count "+3 more" like mail clients. ensures important channels are visible.
Juno Park: accessibility follow-up: when reordering channels via keyboard we need a live update message so screen reader knows the new order: "Email moved to position 2". don't rely on focus change only.
Eli Torres: small CSS tweak to reduce perceived density without changing spacing: reduce the border radius on input pills and slightly increase font-weight for labels. makes things look less cramped. here's a sample CSS we tried:
```
.rule-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; gap: 12px; align-items: center; }
.threshold-pill { border-radius: 6px; font-weight: 600; padding: 6px 8px; }
```
Priya Nair: UX question re: suppression scheduling: users mentioned they expect named schedules ("Weekend quiet") rather than anonymous rules. should we add a name field with optional description? that's more content but helps reuse.
Ben Howard: yes to named schedules. and expose a small preview timestamp on the rule card like "until Sun 9am". reduces confusion.
notify-preview-bot: preview snapshot for thread 1804445555 generated  result: WARN (contrast 1 fail, focus order check 1 warn)
Juno Park: noted the focus-order warn. I'll run a keyboard only pass tomorrow and file a small accessibility checklist.
Eli Torres: i'll prototype the two-column layout and compact summary chip in Figma later today.
Priya Nair: thanks! I'll update the copy doc and we can decide whether to use 'Send notifications to' or 'Notification channels' in the next sync. moving to board column: design-review. :white_check_mark:
